newsitem.title: CHINA: China police hold anti-smuggling drills.
newsitem.headline: China police hold anti-smuggling drills.

text.p: The Chinese People's Armed Police held naval exercises last week aimed at honing the paramilitary group's ability to battle smuggling, the Liberation Army Daily said on Monday.

The Zhejiang border patrol division of the People's Armed Police, which is responsible for 2,800 km (1,740 miles) of coastline, held the exercises off the eastern province of Zhejiang last Friday, the newspaper said. The exercises included weapons practice and search drills.

"These exercises carried out by formations of anti-smuggling ships...fully revealed the comprehensive anti-smuggling capabilities of this division at sea and the fearless bearing of the officers and troops," it said.
The division had cracked more than 1,700 smuggling cases in the past several years, confiscating 12 foreign ships and 300 million yuan ($36 million) in illicit funds, it said.
Smuggling of goods ranging from drugs to stolen cars is rampant along China's thriving and porous coastal areas, including Zhejiang, near the city of Shanghai.
